questions.question: dict lookup average O(1) kyun hota hai, list ki tarah scan kyun nahi karta?
questions.answer: Key ka hash nikalkar us bucket me direct jump karta hai (hash table), isliye list jaisa linear scan nahi lagta. Worst case (sab hash collide) O(n) ho jaata hai, par average O(1) rehta hai.
questions.explanation: Hash + bucket = direct jump.

questions.question: Membership check ke liye dict ya set list se better kab hota hai?

questions.explanation: Lookup-heavy = dict/set.

questions.question: Python 3.7 se dict insertion order guarantee karta hai — practical fayda kya hai?
questions.answer: Output/JSON ka order deterministic hota hai, isliye tests stable rehte hain aur config ki key order maintain hoti hai. Pehle OrderedDict ki zarurat padti thi, ab plain dict kaafi hai.
questions.explanation: Deterministic output = stable tests.

questions.question: 'Key must be hashable' ka matlab kya hai?
questions.answer: Key ke liye __hash__ aur __eq__ consistent hone chahiye — yani immutable values (str, int, tuple) keys ban sakti hain, mutable (list, set, dict) nahi, kyunki badalne par hash badal jaata aur lookup toot jaata.
